Elaine / Jasmine — ran the numbers on the telemetry. Assumptions: 420 avg tokens, 95% requests under 1,000 tokens, model quantized to int8 profile; using cluster-equivalent A100-80GB perf.

High level recommendation (conservative buffer to cover Q4 ramp + headroom):
- Dedicated reserved pool: +10 GPUs (A100-eq) to be provisioned at renewal start (Sep 1).
- Expected sustained throughput (reserved pool): ~1,600 tokens/sec (~3.8 qps @ avg tokens) per GPU for batched inference; with 10 GPUs steady throughput ~16k tokens/sec which covers projected steady + cushion.
- Peak burst model: add access to 6-gpu burst pool (on-demand) for <3 months during major campaign launch windows.

Cost/term tradeoffs:
- 12-month commitment: ~15% discount vs monthly reserved billing.
- 24-month: additional 8% discount + higher SLA uptime window.

I attached a short PDF with the per-hour throughput curves and sensitivity to avg token size. Happy to walk through on the call.

Attachment: citrine-q4-q1-gpu-recs.pdf

Cheers,

Elaine
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -0700

Elaine — thanks for the additional detail. Per your latency SLO and token tail, we updated the sizing and ran a simulated workload. Key points: 

1) Recommended committed configuration (Renewal start Sep 1):
- Reserved pool: 12 GPUs (A100-eq) to provide sustained throughput headroom. This adds ~20% overhead vs Ben’s conservative 10 GPU ask to absorb token tail and p95 variability.
- Burst pool: 6 GPUs accessible via on-demand bursting with pre-authorized capacity (billing at burst rate)

2) Mapped throughput guarantees (business hours 08:00–20:00 ET):
- Committed sustained qps guarantee: 140 qps sustained at average token size (420) across reserved pool (12 GPUs). This maps to ~58k tokens/sec sustained headroom.
- p99 latency guardrails: with 12 GPUs + intelligent KV-prefix caching we expect p99 Interactive < 3.2s for the model family; p95 comfortably below 2.5s in normal conditions.

3) Mid-term expansion:
- We can add reserved GPUs mid-term with 4–6 week lead time for capacity procurement and provisioning in Dedicated. Short-term temporary reserved add-ons (min 3-month commitment) are possible sooner if you accept a provisional price uplift.

4) Next steps I recommend we capture in a mutual action plan: acceptance of committed GPU count, agreed SLA windows and throughput numbers, PO + signature cadence, and a staggered activation plan for burst windows (we can prestage images to reduce warmup).

Attached: mutual-action-plan-citrine.docx

If this aligns, Jasmine — can you capture the commercial term (12 vs 24 months) so I can produce an SLA + pricing worksheet?

Best,
Laura Bennett
